routes.title: The distributive property: why the outside factor reaches every term | Better Grades
routes.metaDescription: Distribution is multiplication across a sum. It expands an expression without changing its value—and it works in reverse when factoring.

routes.metaDescription: An equation stays true when the same legal operation is applied to both sides. Simplify, isolate, and check.

routes.title: Variables on both sides: which side should you move them to? | Better Grades
routes.metaDescription: Either side can work. Choose the direction that keeps the variable coefficient positive and the arithmetic easy to audit.

routes.title: Slope is a rate of change, not just rise over run | Better Grades
routes.metaDescription: Slope measures how much the output changes for each one-unit change in the input. Its sign, size, and units all carry meaning.

routes.title: How to write a line equation from two points | Better Grades
routes.metaDescription: Find the slope first, anchor it to either point, then convert forms only if the problem needs a different presentation.

routes.title: Point-slope or slope-intercept form: which should you use? | Better Grades
routes.metaDescription: Use point-slope form when a point and slope are given; use slope-intercept form when the intercept or a quick graph is the main goal.

routes.metaDescription: Parallel nonvertical lines share a slope. Perpendicular nonvertical lines have slopes whose product is −1—but vertical and horizontal lines need separate language.

routes.title: What do slope and intercept mean in a linear model? | Better Grades
routes.metaDescription: The intercept is the modeled output at input zero; the slope is the predicted change in output per unit of input. Context decides whether either interpretation is sensible.

routes.title: Multiplying polynomials without losing a term | Better Grades

routes.title: Factor the greatest common factor before anything fancy | Better Grades

routes.title: Direct or inverse variation: which model matches the relationship? | Better Grades

routes.title: Solving radical equations and checking for extraneous roots | Better Grades

routes.title: Rational exponents: the bridge between powers and roots | Better Grades
